clue.text: Belts as a Christmas present

definitions.meaning: to belt someone is to punch them hard, as a verb meaning hits
a pair of hosiery is the classic dull gift found under the tree

explanation.surface: Someone is given a pair of trouser belts as a festive gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: a verb for landing hard punches, and the woolly footwear traditionally given at Christmas.

clue.text: Running sap, a tree's branches

indicators.note: running sap flows and shifts, so these letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Sap flows through a tree's limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To branch is to split off or divide, a verb synonym; 'it separates' and 'it branches' mean the same.

clue.text: Pass round a recipe for Noel

indicators.note: the pass is placed round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take', used on prescriptions)

explanation.surface: Someone hands round a recipe to a person named Noel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noel' looks like a man's name, but it is a Christmas song, as in 'The First Noel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noel is a festive hymn sung at Christmas, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: His Christmas present was one of three

definitions.text: His Christmas present was one of three

parts.words: His Christmas present was one of three
parts.note: in Dickens's A Christmas Carol the miser is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come; the second is one of three

explanation.surface: A man received one of a set of three gifts for Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas present' reads as a gift, but it is the Ghost of Christmas Present, one of three spirits in Dickens's story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens miser is the man visited by three spirits, including the Ghost of Christmas Present.

clue.text: One blows top, given plastic tree

parts.note: to top is to beat or outdo, which is to trump

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the following word is reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper on being handed an artificial Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows top' reads as losing one's temper, but 'One blows' is the definition and 'top' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a brass horn produces sound by blowing into the instrument.

clue.text: Carry around attorney until 23rd December?

indicators.note: the word for carry goes around the attorney's letters

parts.note: to tote is to carry
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A lawyer is to be carried about until two days before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle was published on 23 December 2016, so 'until 23rd December' meant up to the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to now; on the day of publication now was 23rd December, hence the question mark.

clue.text: River on clan chief's compound

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
a thane was a Scottish clan chief or lord, as in Macbeth

explanation.surface: A Scottish chieftain's property stands beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' reads as an enclosed estate, but it is a chemical compound. 'on' just places the river first in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chemical compound, used in making plastics and varnishes; the definition names the class.

clue.text: Neat whiskey keeps this clue within reach

indicators.note: the word for neat keeps the clue number held within it

parts.note: neat drink is pure, undiluted
this clue is 6-down, and 6 in Roman numerals is VI
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A glass of neat whiskey is kept close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue' refers to its own number, 6, written as Roman VI.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope or range of authority or view is one's reach; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Sides to keep interrupting over tie that's happened

indicators.note: the letter for over breaks into the run of side letters, splitting it
the sides of a word are its first and last letters, here of the two words to and keep

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
to lace is to tie, as with shoes

explanation.surface: Teams persist in disrupting a cricket over that ended in a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' gives T, O from 'to' and K, P from 'keep'; 'interrupting' puts O between TO and KP. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurred is said to have happened; the phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Take home Christmas card feature?

parts.note: to rob is to take unlawfully
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone collects a Christmas card to carry indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted songbird is a familiar picture on British Christmas cards, so it is an example of a card's feature.

clue.text: Leave band a unique Christmas present

parts.note: to part is to leave
a ridge is a raised band or strip

explanation.surface: A band quits to give an unusual Christmas gift.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' the gift of the first day comes singly, 'in a pear tree', unlike all the later gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Only one game bird is given in the carol, so it is the unique present among many.

clue.text: Diamond in right hand, groom's heading off

indicators.note: the first letter of the groom word is taken off

parts.note: to comb is to groom hair; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A bride's diamond is held in the groom's right hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' wants to be a bridegroom, but it is a verb, to comb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus or diamond shape is a parallelogram with four equal sides; this is its shorter name.

clue.text: Start off Christmas in defeat? Don't let that happen!

indicators.note: the shortened Christmas word goes in the word for defeat

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat

indicators.note: the first letter of the Christmas word is taken off

parts.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas

explanation.surface: Losing the start of Christmas would be a disaster that must be prevented.
explanation.definitionFit: As a command the phrasal verb means exclude a possibility, so it says prevent that outcome.

clue.text: One fastens locks very tight

definitions.meaning: locks of hair are held in place by a slender bent clip
a very sharp bend in a road is so called, as in a ... bend

explanation.surface: A device that secures locks very firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors and keys, but it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent wire clip holds hair, and the same word describes an extremely sharp road bend.

clue.text: Can almost handle Christmas decoration

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to handle goods is to sell them, as a shop does

explanation.surface: Someone can just about cope with Christmas decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering strips of metallic foil are hung on trees as a festive ornament.

clue.text: Santa's home help — or not, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Santa wonders whether his home help will turn up or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home help' reads as a domestic helper, but 'home' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is said to live at the top of the world, his traditional home.

clue.text: Cocktail party — I wrap up Christmas present first

indicators.note: first says the Christmas and present pieces come before the party
the final letter speaks as the one that wraps up, or ends, the word

parts.note: now is the present time
a ball is a dancing party

explanation.surface: At a cocktail party, someone wraps a Christmas gift before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas present' looks like a gift, but it splits: its last letter S, then NOW for 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed drink of advocaat and lemonade is a specific cocktail, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Obstruction in toilet potentially making one wee on foot

indicators.note: the obstruction goes in the rearranged letters
potentially says the letters could form something else

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A blocked toilet threatens to make someone urinate on their own foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges TOILET into LITTOE, and 'in' puts LET inside it. 'wee' looks like urinating but means small.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest digit on the foot is a tiny one; wee is Scottish for small.

clue.text: Santa's team drops 25 audibly

indicators.note: audibly means the words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: drops of water are rain, and 25 is the answer to 25-down, a heavenly being; a sweet person is a dear, so this pair says rain dear

explanation.surface: Santa's helpers let fall a number of items.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' refers to the answer to 25-down, an angel, which is a term of endearment like 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's sleigh is pulled by a team of antlered animals, Rudolph and company.

clue.text: Ship carrying right Christmas decoration

indicators.note: the ship carries the right letter inside it

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship

explanation.surface: A vessel transports the right sort of festive decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A long paper ribbon hung or thrown at parties is a typical festive decoration.

clue.text: When drunk, ban this liqueur

indicators.note: being drunk muddles things, so these letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker says this green spirit should be prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: This green wormwood spirit is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, an example of the class.

clue.text: For some, the present opening is the first sign of Christmas

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the present era for those who count years that way
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: Some people think opening presents is what first signals Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the present opening' reads as unwrapping gifts, but splits into the present era and an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season of four weeks leading to Christmas Day heralds the festival's approach.

clue.text: With dad gone, is this on one's wish list?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: de- means removed, and sired means fathered, so something unfathered

explanation.surface: A child asks whether, with Dad gone, this is what they asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as DE-SIRED, the father taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything on a wish list is wanted or longed for, a plain synonym.

clue.text: More than one way to wrap tiny stocking filler

indicators.note: the ways wrap round the tiny word

parts.note: ST is street, a way, so two is STS
wee is Scottish for tiny

explanation.surface: Several ways to gift-wrap a small item for a Christmas stocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery is typically stuffed into a Christmas stocking, so it is an example of a filler.

clue.text: Can thus name president

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
so means thus

explanation.surface: A question of whether one can name a president this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb, but it is US slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew and Lyndon B. were both US presidents with this surname.

clue.text: Short gag about fine Christmas cracker contents

indicators.note: the shortened gag goes about the word for fine
short means cut off the last letter

parts.note: a gag is a jest
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A brief joke about a fine is found in a Christmas cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts JEST to JES, and 'about' wraps it round OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper crackers pulled at Christmas dinner contain groan-worthy one-liners along with a hat and a toy.

clue.text: Moan about idiot's Christmas song

indicators.note: the moan goes about the idiot

parts.note: to wail is to moan
an ass is an idiot; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a fool's festive singing.
explanation.definitionFit: An old drinking toast sung door to door at Yuletide is a traditional Christmas song.

clue.text: An upturned stocking filler, one on Christmas tree

indicators.note: upturned in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a leg is what fills a stocking

explanation.surface: A gift from a stocking is turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking filler' looks like a small gift, but is a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A winged heavenly figure often sits atop a Christmas tree as its crowning ornament.

clue.text: Extremely keen to have patent

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: An inventor is very eager to hold a patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like a noun, but is the adjective meaning plain or obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means evident or obvious, so widely recognised.

clue.text: It has small flowers (they're big when out)

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A plant with tiny blooms that open up large.
explanation.definitionFit: This low meadow herb, Euphrasia, bears small white flowers once used for eye remedies.

clue.text: Crooked men working at night during Christmas?

definitions.text: Crooked men working at night during Christmas?

parts.words: Crooked men working at night during Christmas?
parts.note: the carol tells how flock-watchers worked by night at the Nativity; they carry crooks, so they are crooked men

explanation.surface: Criminals working the night shift over Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonesty but means carrying a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Flock-keepers watched sheep by night, as the carol says, carrying hooked staffs.

clue.text: Search of Lapland elves

indicators.note: of here means taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A hunt carried out by elves from Lapland.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig deep into something is to search or investigate it.
